what_worked: Consistent dark-theme visual identity with clear hierarchy and legible pink-accent typography throughout the deck.
fix_next: Replace every fabricated statistic with verifiable dataset figures; disclose missingness, sample sizes, and limitations for a cold reader.
verdict: Polished template over fabricated data; reads as generic VC playbook, not a data story.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: 'LTV Predictability Index' chart is entirely fabricated—no such metric exists in the dataset. Slide 5: 60/18/12/10% business model split is invented; dataset categories are AI, Marketing, E-comm, SaaS, etc. Slide 5: '60%+ SaaS & Subscription' claim unverifiable. Slide 8: Stripe 71.43% and RevenueCat 21.43% shares are wrong (actual: Stripe 636/875≈72.7%, RevenueCat 189/875≈21.6%—close but the '75% combined' text claim rounds misleadingly and Dodo at 4.76% overstates its 50/875≈5.7% share). Slide 9: Churn, capital efficiency, and valuation multiple table is generic industry boilerplate with no dataset backing. Slide 10: 'Top 10% drive 80%+ of revenue' is fabricated—actual top-10 share is ~49.6%. Slide 10: Correlation coefficients (DR↔Subscriptions 0.45, Visitors↔Subscriptions 0.82) are unverifiable and likely invented. Slide 10: '6.25% total conversion rate' has no derivation shown. Slide 10: 'DR 30+ tipping point' claim unsupported. Slide 12: Investment allocation pie (30/25/20/15/10%) is a recommendation chart with no data basis and is partially cut off.

evidence.insight: No dataset-specific discoveries surfaced: misses Education's high median ($2,435), anonymous revenue share (26.5%), near-zero founded-year correlation (r=0.025), .ai vs .com median gap, or actual top-10 concentration (49.6%). Tier rankings on slide 7 and buy recommendations on slide 11 are opinion without shown evidence.
evidence.narrative: Loose investment-thesis arc exists (landscape → drivers → categories → picks) but every slide restates 'double down on B2B SaaS' without building cumulative evidence, introducing tension, or synthesizing findings. No landing slide ties back to data.
evidence.framing: Audience is implied as investor/allocator but dataset provenance, time window, revenue definition, and critical missingness (241 country, 274 category, 288 audience_type, 216 zero-revenue rows) are never disclosed. A cold reader cannot assess any claim's reliability.
evidence.accuracy: Multiple statistics are fabricated or unverifiable: the LTV index, business-model split, 80%+ skew claim, correlation coefficients, conversion rate, valuation multiples, and churn ratings. The dataset's actual category taxonomy is replaced with invented categories. Slide 8 payment shares are approximately close but text rounds misleadingly.
evidence.visual: Dark theme with pink accents is consistent and legible. Chart types are appropriate in principle. However, charts visualize fabricated data, decorative AI illustrations consume ~40% of slides 1, 2, 4, 6 without informational value, and slide 12's pie chart is cut off at the bottom.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive consulting jargon ('monetization engine,' 'distribution flywheel,' 'capital deployment,' 'organic distribution flywheels,' 'de facto infrastructure standard'). Decorative AI-generated illustrations on slides 1, 2, 4, 6. Slide 9 is a generic SaaS industry framework pasted without dataset evidence. The entire deck could describe any startup dataset without modification.

change_reason: Lowered accuracy from 2.5 to 2.0: on closer review, the fabricated 80%+ skew claim (actual ~49.6%) and invented correlation coefficients represent more serious data integrity failures than initially weighted. Lowered framing from 3.0 to 2.5: complete absence of missingness disclosure and dataset provenance is more damaging for a cold reader than preliminary score reflected. Other dimensions confirmed.
